calls.head: Turnovers could swing this one
calls.body: The Rangers turn stolen pucks into chances, and the Lightning are near the bottom of the league at avoiding breakdowns. A sloppy pass or two could cost the Lightning.
calls.call: The Rangers get at least their usual 7.5% of their 5-on-5 chances right after winning the puck.
calls.nums: NY Rangers 10th for chances off turnovers (7.5% of their chances come right after winning the puck) · Tampa Bay 24th for avoiding breakdowns

calls.happened: 3.3% of NY Rangers’s 5-on-5 chances came right after winning the puck, against their usual 7.5%.

calls.head: Good looks against hopeful ones
calls.body: The Lightning are near the top of the league for shot quality, at the dangerous end; the Rangers are near the bottom of the league, at the hopeful end. Expect that gap to show.
calls.call: The Lightning’s shots are more dangerous on average than the Rangers’.

surprises.head: NY Rangers shut down Tampa Bay’s power play
surprises.body: Tampa Bay’s power play created 2.6 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.5 and a league average of 7.5. A team strays this far about once every 15 games.

surprises.head: Tampa Bay leaned on their bottom six
surprises.body: Tampa Bay’s bottom-six forwards played 44% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 41% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 10 games.

story.head: The Rangers roll past the Lightning
paras: Mika Zibanejad opened the scoring early in the first. Five different Rangers scored.
The chances were closer than the score.

items.text: None of the preview’s two calls held.
